chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Rifāʿah, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding:
The man who dies having no inheritor and no master—he عليه السلام said: “He is among the people meant by this verse.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man in question whose estate is being discussed
key_terms.الْآيَةِ: the Qur’anic verse being cited as proof
key_terms.الْأَنْفَالِ: properties classified as al-anfāl, belonging to a special legal category
key_terms.مَوْلَى: a master or patron with legal claim
key_terms.وَارِثَ: an inheritor entitled to receive the estate
key_terms.يَمُوتُ: dies; the legal situation begins upon his death

ai.seo_question: What happens in Shia hadith to the property of a person who dies without any heir?
ai.summary: This hadith applies the Qur’anic category of al-anfāl to the estate of a person who dies without an heir and without a master. It indicates that such ownerless property falls under the domain referenced by the verse about al-anfāl, linking inheritance law to Qur’anic classification of certain properties.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Rifa’at, from Aban Bin Taghlub,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the man who is dying and there is no inheritor for him, nor a master. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be from the rightful ones of this Verse
[Shakir 8:1] They are asking you about the spoils of war’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayar from Shu‘ayb from abu al-Sabbah who has said the following. “Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said to me,
“We are the people obedience to whom is obligatory by the commands of Allah.
Al-Anfal (properties acquired without the use of armed forces) and the best of the properties of the gains from war belong to us.”
